THE THIRD REVIEW OF 1.24.31 (MAKE STATION: AI_STATION; the floatless duplex and the two alarm lights in AI_CONTROL;
grammarFor / fixKind / wholeFor in AI_ACTIONS; the small mends in AI_PUMP_STATION and AI_PARTS). Reviewed at 629b9b7 by
a reviewer that did not write the rules and did not read the first two reviews (station_review1_1231,
station_review2_1231). 1.24.30 (ad0d654) loaded beside it for every comparison.

HOW TO REPLAY
  node tests/fixtures/station_review3_1231/replay.js [id-prefix]     (jsdom, about 10 s; needs git for ad0d654)
  Grammar results (F) are read from grammar_results.json. To remake them:
    node tests/fixtures/station_review3_1231/make_grammar.js > tests/fixtures/station_review3_1231/grammar_cases.json
    python3 tools/gbnf_check.py --lib <llama.cpp b11435>/libllama.so --vocab ggml-vocab-qwen2.gguf \
      tests/fixtures/station_review3_1231/grammar_cases.json --out tests/fixtures/station_review3_1231/grammar_results.json
  F-01 fails if the grammars there are no longer the ones Lantern writes (a stale result is not read as a pass).
  load.js and sim.js are copies of ../liftstation_review3_1230/ (read before use); lib.js and every case are this
  review's own. Harm: high = a wrong station or circuit drawn, or a right one replaced, with nothing said or sent back;
  medium = a misreading said but not mended, a wrong line handed back, a right drawing lost, or a tool offered that
  invites the wrong answer; low = wording, odd writing, a miss that 1.24.30 had too.

COUNTS
  A over-reach (bench guard, plain questions, other machines, right circuits, mends)  59 cases, 22 DISAGREE (5 high, 12 medium, 5 low)
  B questions in parts, stray blocks                                                  24 cases,  5 DISAGREE (1 medium, 4 low)
  C counts of pumps and float lines                                                   58 cases, 15 DISAGREE (7 high, 6 medium, 2 low)
  D blocks that disagree (the drawings' own blocks read as a station)                 19 cases,  8 DISAGREE (2 high, 4 medium, 2 low)
  E every sentence against what was drawn (simulated)                                 24 cases,  4 DISAGREE (3 medium, 1 low)
  F grammars through llama.cpp's parser; when a grammar is sent                       27 cases,  3 DISAGREE (3 low)
  In all: 211 cases: 154 AGREE, 57 DISAGREE (14 high, 26 medium, 17 low), in 14 root causes below.

FINDINGS, MOST HARM FIRST

1. HIGH. The question's "one pump" laid over a right block's two (C-23, C-24, C-25 high; C-26 medium).
   countsIn() takes "one pump" as the question's count wherever it stands, and spec() overrules the block when the
   question names one count. "Design a lift station where each pump can handle the peak flow with one pump out of
   service" -- the duplex rule the station's own UNKNOWN line quotes -- with "pumps 2" is drawn as ONE pump, the lag
   float dropped ("1 pump: the question asks for 1 (the block said 2)"). Same for "one pump running and one standby
   pump", "if one pump fails the other takes over", "runs one pump at a time". The redundancy the question asks for is
   removed from a right block. Rule 7: "one pump" in out of service / standby / fails / at a time is not a count.

2. HIGH. A rating before the count read as the count (C-16..C-19 high; C-20, C-21, C-22 medium).
   The first number on a pumps line is taken: "pumps 5 HP x 2" = 5 pumps, "pumps 15 kW x 2" = 15, "pumps 150 gpm, 2 of
   them" = 150 (the levels drawn with P1..P150, nothing else), "pumps 480 V, 2" = 480, "pumps 3 phase, 2 pumps" = 3
   (no control drawn), "pumps 10 HP each, 2 total" = 10; "pumps 1 + 1" = 1 (a simplex). Only "said" ("the usual floats
   for 150 pumps"), never sent back. A number with a unit after it (HP, kW, gpm, L/s, V, phase) is not a count.

3. HIGH. Other machines at a sewage works or storm station read as a pump station (A-17..A-27; A-57 high).
   asks() = a wet-well word (sewage, wastewater, sewer, storm water) + two drawings. NOT_OURS lists none of: blower,
   generator, sampler, vacuum, gate, press, UV, trash rake, digester/mixing, truck. Each of 11 such questions is offered
   MAKE STATION alone (1.24.30 offered the control and piping tools). Worse in Chat (A-57): the model's right blower
   starter is answered "the question asks for a pump station", the next call is held to the STATION grammar, and the
   turn ends with a duplex pump station. Rule 7: ask what else the machine named can be; act only when it is the pumps.

4. HIGH. A phantom alarm float when the control and the levels name one float in two wordings (D-03, D-04).
   MAKE CONTROL "float FS4 "alarm"" beside MAKE LEVELS "float FS4 "high level alarm" 5 ft" (or FS3 "alarm" / "high water
   alarm"): spec() keeps two alarms with different labels as two floats, the second tag is renumbered (FS5), and the
   station lists FS5 as a part, says "If the water reaches FS5 (high level alarm), nothing drawn comes on" and "Lift FS5:
   nothing drawn comes on" -- a float in neither drawing, an alarm with no signal. The clash check compares jobs (same:
   no clash), so ok is true, nothing is said, nothing goes back. Same tag + same job = one float.

5. HIGH/MEDIUM. The floatless-duplex mend adds four floats where something already starts the pumps (A-42 high;
   A-43, A-44 medium). The rule asks only "no float at all, wet-well words, the coils are pumps". A duplex whose calls come
   from a level controller's contacts (switch SS1 CR1 / SS2 CR2) gets FS1 and FS2 around CR1 in series with SS1, and a
   second lag relay CR3 beside the model's CR2. A hand-started duplex (stop PB1 / start PB2 CR1) gets FS1 in series with
   the stop: the start button does nothing in a dry well. A call button likewise. 1.24.30 sent these back once. Rule 7:
   act only when nothing else starts the call.

6. MEDIUM. A levels correction throws away the control the model wrote (D-12 Chat, D-13 bench path; D-14 low).
   MAKE CONTROL (24 V DC, a horn) + MAKE LEVELS with FS1 above FS2 goes back as MAKE LEVELS (fixKind, its grammar). The
   corrected MAKE LEVELS is then built alone (ctx.text is the new reply only): the station's control is Lantern's usual
   (L1/L2, run lights, no horn) and it says "Lantern assumed: no control voltage". The note before it says "Lantern
   checked the MAKE CONTROL block: the float levels: ..." (D-14).

7. MEDIUM. Lines handed back that are not right for THIS block (rule 3) (D-02, D-11 medium; D-19, C-56 low).
   D-02: the disagreement's line gives FS1, FS2, FS4 heights and FS3 none; copied, it comes back ("give every float its
   height ... or none"). D-11: a simplex MAKE CONTROL for a duplex question goes back as MAKE STATION (grammar STATION)
   with MAKE CONTROL lines ("alternator AR M1 M2, coil M1 ...") and the words "Lantern checked your MAKE STATION block";
   the station's own line is "pumps 2". D-19: two pumps each on its own float, no alternator: "float FS3 M1" for pump 2's
   float (1.24.30's MAKE CONTROL text, now inside a station). C-56: "give FS2 a height above -2 ft" for "lead-3ft".

8. MEDIUM. The parts list leaves out parts of a control the model wrote (E-20, E-24).
   partsList() reads starters, overloads, control relays, the alternator, lights and horns. A selector switch (the
   35B's own SS1 "lead/lag select"), a control fuse, an E-stop and a lamp-test button are drawn and not listed.

9. MEDIUM/LOW. "How", "why", "should" and "explain" questions offered MAKE STATION alone (A-11, A-12 medium; A-13..A-16
   low). "How do I design a lift station?", "Should I design my lift station with two pumps or three?", "Can you explain
   the sequence of operation ...", "What does a lift station parts list usually include?": 1.24.30 offered no tool.
   Chat does not push for a block on these (one call, checked), so the harm is the prompt's "Reply with ONE block",
   which a small model copies.

10. MEDIUM. Float lines read in part, the rest only "not read" (C-53, C-54 medium; C-55 low).
   "Off float 2 ft / Lead float 3 ft / Lag float 4 ft / Alarm float 5 ft": only the alarm line is read (its first word is
   a role word); the lag float is dropped, the heights lost (not to scale), nothing goes back. "floats: redundant off,
   off, lead, lag, alarm": the redundant off merged into the off float, unsaid (MAKE CONTROL keeps two off floats).
   "LSL off / LSH lead on / LSHH alarm": not read, and the usual four drawn -- a lag float the block did not have.

11. MEDIUM. How it works tells of a part not drawn or listed (E-09; E-08 low).
   A two-pump station shown without its control ("show piping levels") still says "Each time the pumps stop, the
   alternating relay changes over" -- no alternating relay is drawn or in the parts list (alternates() falls back to
   count === 2). E-08: a simplex's alarm sentence says "the pumps are not keeping up. One may have failed".

12. MEDIUM/LOW. Questions in parts (B-10 medium; B-02, B-04, B-09, B-11 low).
   B-10: "..., then make a table of the float heights" is read whole as the station (views() takes "float heights" as
   the levels): no table is made, nothing says so (1.24.30 made CONTROL+PIPING+SHEET). B-02/B-04: the merged STATION
   part's text carries the next part's tail into what the model is shown ("1. Draw the control circuit for the city
   council, the piping ..."; "control circuit of the pump run hours, piping"). B-09: a station beside a conveyor's
   starter is not merged (CONTROL+PIPING+CONTROL, as 1.24.30), unlike a station beside a house or a deck. B-11: two
   stations asked for, one made, the other unsaid.

13. LOW. Grammar edges (F-08, F-09, F-10). "2 pumps" and "Two submersible pumps", which the parser reads, are held out
   (no number or "two" among the first words). Prose that starts with a role word passes ("Pump 1 and pump 2 take turns,
   so they wear evenly.", "Floats are set by ..."), and the first is read as ONE pump (finding 2's rule).

14. LOW. The height-from-the-label mend loses inch heights written before the label (A-58): float FS1 24" "off" was
   24 in on 1.24.30, now no height (drawn not to scale).

WHAT HELD (selected)
  - Over-reach guard: all 298 other bench questions get 1.24.30's tools, split and prompt (A-01); only the two lift
    stations are stations (A-02); every other bench ideal solves and grades as on 1.24.30 (A-03); the 284 distinct model
    replies kept in tests/fixtures/bench_run_*.json build (A-04), grade on the bench's path (A-55) and run in Chat (A-56)
    exactly as on 1.24.30 -- the one change being that 39 of those Chat turns' corrections now carry their kind's
    grammar (MUSIC, DRAWING, CODE, CARDS, DOC, WHEEL), and every bench ideal of 15 kinds passes its own kind's grammar
    in llama.cpp (F-27).
  - Right circuits unchanged: a motor starter, the instructions' duplex, compressors on pressure switches, a simplex
    sump, forward/reverse; fans and blowers on an alternator get no floats; the two-alarm-light mend puts each light on
    its own float (A-39) and leaves a single shared light as it was (A-40).
  - Fifteen ways of writing the pump count and twenty-five of writing the floats are read right (C).
  - Disagreements on a float's job, a float only in the levels, a piping of another count: said or sent back (D-01,
    D-05, D-09); levels alone, piping alone, a MAKE SCHEMATIC of control lines read as the station; a fan's starter not.
  - Sentences true of the simulated control: the usual duplex (lead held to off, the turns, both on the lag, the alarm),
    simplex, a low level alarm's amber light, a lag pump's own off float, two alarms with the horn on the high-high,
    24 V DC, plug valves, three and five pumps, the Writer document's sections, the no-alarm line (E).
  - Grammars: llama.cpp parses all 31; Lantern's own CONTROL, PIPING and LEVELS blocks pass; fifteen writings of a
    right MAKE STATION pass and ten non-blocks are held (preface, fences, bold, sentences, text after END, no title, a
    second block); the lines Lantern hands back pass the grammar the correction is held to; the 0.8B's copied guide is
    held. The first call never carries a grammar, a server that is not llama.cpp gets none, a correction naming another
    kind gets none.
  - Mixed questions in Chat and on the bench's path: station then slides, sheet, code; house then station; a stray
    block for the station part, or for a whole station question, asked for once with the STATION grammar and no more.

NOT RUN OR NOT CHECKED
  - No model was run. Every reply is scripted; the grammars were checked with llama.cpp's parser token by token
    (gbnf_check.py, libllama b11435, a Qwen2 vocabulary), not by generation. Whether a small model held to a grammar
    (EOS allowed only after END) loops on blank or "note" lines until max_tokens was not run.
  - A grammar with the Qwen3.5 template and enable_thinking false on a live llama-server: not run.
  - No drawing was rendered or looked at (no browser run); the levels drawing of C-18 (150 pumps) was not looked at.
  - The standards the checks, parts list and "does not know" lines cite (Ten States 2014, Ontario 7.2.5, OSHA
    1910.146/.147, 1926 Subpart AA, Hydromatic S3R/S3RX) were not re-read on their pages by this reviewer; only that
    each sentence matches what was drawn.
  - An inlet invert below the lag and alarm floats is drawn without a word (MAKE LEVELS, 1.24.30's); not judged, no
    source opened.
  - A server that refuses a grammar (400), and the page without AI_STATION, are in tests/station.js; not repeated.
  - The PDF save and the "in Draw" buttons were not pressed.
  - The first and second reviews' cases were not read, so overlaps with them are not known.
